T: Be our guest. Bring an appetite.
D: A bookish young woman takes her father's place as the Beast's prisoner in his enchanted castle.
P: Serve the mains when Lumière throws Belle a dinner show in the castle dining room.
S: Toasted baguette with brie and apple, or goat's cheese and honey
Baguette slices toasted with olive oil, topped with brie and apple, or goat's cheese and honey, laid out on a wooden board.
Boiled eggs with a Dijon, mayo and chive yolk filling, dusted with paprika

Eggs boiled 10 minutes, yolks mashed with mayo, Dijon and chives, piped back in and dusted with paprika, a big platter of them. Boil 12 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel. Halve and mash the yolks with mayonnaise, Dijon and snipped chives until smooth. Pipe back into the whites and dust with smoked paprika. Pile onto one big platter, because no one eats eggs like Gaston.
Mrs Potts and Chip serving tea

Crustless finger sandwiches of curried coronation chicken with apricot and almonds, and cucumber with cream cheese, on a tiered stand. Shred 400g roast chicken. Mix 4 tbsp mayo, 2 tbsp Greek yoghurt, 2 tsp mild curry powder, 1 tbsp apricot jam, 40g toasted flaked almonds and chopped coriander, then fold through the chicken. Spread 12 slices of soft bread with butter. Make 4 rounds of coronation chicken and 2 of thin cucumber with 100g cream cheese. Trim the crusts and cut each round into 3 fingers.
M: Beef chuck braised with bacon, baby onions and mushrooms

Beef chuck braised slow with bacon, mushrooms and baby onions in a rich, glossy stock, served over buttery mash with crusty bread. Brown 150g diced bacon, then brown 1.2kg diced beef chuck in batches. Add 12 peeled baby onions and 300g mushrooms and colour lightly. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour and 2 tbsp tomato paste, then add 750ml beef stock, 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar, thyme and 2 bay leaves. Cover and simmer for 3 hours. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and warm milk. Serve with crusty bread.
Belle's father Maurice heading off to market

Chicken thighs braised with leeks, thyme, mustard and a splash of cream until tender, with crusty bread to mop up every bit of sauce. Season 1kg chicken thighs and brown skin side down in a little oil for 6 minutes, then turn and remove. Soften 2 sliced leeks in 20g butter, add 2 crushed garlic cloves and thyme, then pour in 300ml chicken stock and 1 tbsp Dijon mustard. Return the chicken, cover and simmer for 30 minutes. Stir in 100ml cream and bubble for 5 minutes. Serve with crusty bread.
W: Sweet pastry case with custard and thin red apple slices in circles
Sweet pastry blind baked, filled with vanilla custard, topped with thin apple slices fanned into a rose and glazed with apricot jam.
K: Peach nectar and orange juice with sliced orange and fresh peach

Peach nectar, orange and a touch of vanilla topped with sparkling apple juice, glowing gold like Belle's ball gown, with peach slices. In a big jug, mix 750ml chilled peach nectar, the juice of 2 oranges and 1/2 tsp vanilla. Add 1 sliced orange and 1 sliced fresh peach. Just before serving, add plenty of ice and top with 750ml chilled sparkling apple juice. Stir gently and pour into wide glasses so a peach slice lands in each.

steps.text: Slice the baguette and brush with oil.
Toast until golden.
Slice the apples thinly.
Top half with brie and apple, the rest with goat's cheese and a drizzle of honey.
Boil the eggs until hard.
Cool and peel.
Halve the eggs and mash the yolks with mayonnaise, Dijon and chives until smooth.
Pipe back into the whites.
Dust with smoked paprika and pile onto one big platter.
Dice the bacon and beef and peel the baby onions.
Brown the bacon in the olive oil, then brown the beef in batches.
Add the onions and mushrooms and colour lightly.
Stir in the flour and tomato paste, then add the stock, balsamic vinegar, thyme and bay leaves.
Cover and simmer until the beef is tender.
Peel and boil the potatoes, then mash with butter and warm milk.
Serve the braise over the mash with crusty bread.
Cut the mushrooms into big chunks and peel the baby onions.
Brown the mushrooms hard in the oil in batches, dusting the last batch with smoked paprika.
Add the onions and colour lightly.
Stir in the flour and tomato paste, then add the stock, soy sauce, balsamic vinegar, thyme, bay leaves and lentils.
Cover and simmer until the onions are soft and the sauce is thick.
Peel and boil the potatoes, then mash with butter and warm milk.
Serve the braise over the mash with crusty bread.
Line a tart tin with the pastry.
Blind bake at 180C until pale gold.
Cool the case.
Slice the apples paper thin. Squeeze the lemon into the 500 ml of water, soften the slices in it briefly, then drain.
Fill the case with custard.
Arrange the apple slices in overlapping circles into a rose.
Bake at 180C.
Warm the jam with 1 tbsp of water and brush over to glaze.
Cool before slicing.

s.note: Toasted baguette with brie and apple, or goat's cheese and honey
s.how: Slice a baguette, brush with olive oil and toast until golden. Top half with brie and thin slices of red apple. Top the rest with goat's cheese and a drizzle of honey. Lay them out on a wooden board like a village market stall.
